title: DOOMSDAY // FIELD GUIDE
subtitle: Fourteen registered variants. Four evidence layers. No invented winner.

evidence_legend.label: Tournament surface
evidence_legend.meaning: Named stored entrants and records; publication and dependence caveats apply.

evidence_legend.label: Construction / raw seven
evidence_legend.meaning: Exact list composition and hypergeometric opening events; never played-game win rate.

evidence_legend.label: Decision scenario
evidence_legend.meaning: Cross-source interpretation or hypothetical break-even algebra with assumptions visible.

evidence_legend.label: Physical test
evidence_legend.meaning: Preregistered matched-play requirement; this campaign recorded zero played games.

headline.title: Choose the smallest intervention that can earn its slots.
headline.body: Current Dimir is the live control; Personal Tutor is the focused-access benchmark. Green, white, red, and denial packages become preferred tests only when their paired gain clears their field-weighted cost. This is a testing hierarchy, not a power ranking.
headline.secondary_metric_label: played-game results produced by this campaign

recommendation_cards.name: Current Dimir
recommendation_cards.recommendation: Start here and make every larger package beat it in paired play.
recommendation_cards.why: Exact current 75, one 4–2 standings recurrence, six access cards, and a seven-creature sideboard switch.
recommendation_cards.best_when: The room is mixed or uncertain and comparison quality matters.
recommendation_cards.watch: Post-board hands can split between combo and creature plans.

recommendation_cards.name: Personal Tutor turbo
recommendation_cards.recommendation: Use as the focused-access calibration, not as an already proven winner.
recommendation_cards.why: Seven access cards and a 53.906% raw-seven access-plus-black-or-Petal event; exact current recurrence is zero because the nearest publication differs by one sideboard card.
recommendation_cards.best_when: A narrow, direct combo posture is expected to retain value across the room.
recommendation_cards.watch: The raw-seven model does not measure keep quality, combo turn, or interaction.

recommendation_cards.name: Light green-white
recommendation_cards.recommendation: Test before the broader four-color bundle when Veil, Carpet, and creature removal have clear targets.
recommendation_cards.why: Exact current 75, one 3–3 standings recurrence, five access, 15 selection, and a bounded green/white package.
recommendation_cards.best_when: Blue/black interaction, Islands, and relevant creatures overlap in the expected room.
recommendation_cards.watch: Conditional cards and green/white mana must be logged as live, stranded, or costly.

recommendation_cards.name: Wasteland / Murktide
recommendation_cards.recommendation: Build when nonbasic mana and slower games are the declared target; seek an independent pilot.
recommendation_cards.why: The exact lineage is 21–8 after duplicate collapse, but every recurrence is one pilot; 19 lands produce 72.058% two-land raw sevens.
recommendation_cards.best_when: Opposing nonbasic mana is strategically central and a real clock matters.
recommendation_cards.watch: Four access cards, seven acceleration cards, and Wasteland activations can compete with combo resources.

recommendation_cards.name: Esper Teferi / Swords
recommendation_cards.recommendation: Test the compact white value-and-removal intervention before adding green mechanisms.
recommendation_cards.why: Exact current 75 with ten main value/tempo cards; its exact recurrence is one selected League publication with no standings denominator.
recommendation_cards.best_when: Creature boards and permission both demand answers.
recommendation_cards.watch: Four access cards and multicolor sequencing trade raw access for board presence and timing control.

recommendation_cards.name: Grixis Squelcher
recommendation_cards.recommendation: Treat as a current-regime replication of a persistent protection creature.
recommendation_cards.why: The exact historical list has a 7–1 Challenge and one League publication, both from one pilot.
recommendation_cards.best_when: A creature that creates a counter-proof window could attack the expected interaction.
recommendation_cards.watch: No current exact entrant; red mana and creature removal are real exposure points.

playstyle_rows.tempo: Compress resources toward Doomsday; decide when to expose the top-deck Tutor line.
playstyle_rows.advantage: Few game-one cards point away from the combo.
playstyle_rows.risk: A narrow plan may leave opposing combo hate live.

playstyle_rows.tempo: Combo/disrupt game one; choose combo, clock, or both after boarding.
playstyle_rows.mulligan: A functional primary axis without stranded halves.

playstyle_rows.tempo: Time Veil around blue/black interaction and Carpet around opposing Islands.
playstyle_rows.mulligan: Functional green mana plus a live, opponent-relevant payoff.
playstyle_rows.advantage: Targeted stack insulation and conditional mana.
playstyle_rows.risk: Dead conditional cards and splash exposure outside the target class.

playstyle_rows.tempo: Develop creature or planeswalker value before choosing the combo window.
playstyle_rows.mulligan: Functional multicolor mana plus a coherent early action.
playstyle_rows.advantage: Board presence, removal, and response-window control.
playstyle_rows.risk: More mechanisms tax access and complicate attribution.

playstyle_rows.tempo: Resolve a persistent protection creature, then exploit its window or remain on combo.
playstyle_rows.mulligan: Red access plus spells that benefit from the protection window.
playstyle_rows.advantage: Protection and clock in one permanent.
playstyle_rows.risk: Creature removal and unsupported current-field efficacy.

playstyle_rows.tempo: Allocate lands between colored combo mana and Wasteland while applying pressure.
playstyle_rows.mulligan: Functional colored mana plus relevant denial or pressure.
playstyle_rows.advantage: A real mana-denial and clock axis.
playstyle_rows.risk: Self-sacrificed lands and lower access may conflict with combo assembly.

experiments.name: Outcome surface
experiments.result: Current standings total 18–16; no stable variant ordering survives the publication, dependence, and taxonomy caveats.
experiments.measured: Selection channel, Wilson intervals, pilot/event deletion, threshold sensitivity, historical windows, exact recurrence.
experiments.not_measured: Failed League denominator, stable pilot-adjusted effects, or current matchup effects.

experiments.name: Construction / raw seven
experiments.result: Fourteen exact 60/15 artifacts passed hash and legality checks; opening events were enumerated exactly.
experiments.measured: Composition, source allocation, role counts, raw unordered seven-card probabilities.
experiments.not_measured: Mulligans, sequencing, piles, opponent interaction, matchups, or wins.

experiments.name: Scenario economics
experiments.result: Break-even surfaces translate broad-field cost and hostile share into required target-pocket gain.
experiments.measured: Algebraic thresholds under a two-stratum weighted-average assumption.
experiments.not_measured: Any candidate's actual gain or loss.

experiments.name: Paired physical screen
experiments.result: 260 candidate and 260 paired-control matches are allocated; played results remain zero.
experiments.not_measured: Matchup effects, combo turns, alternate-plan conversion, splash costs, and pilot sensitivity.

limitations.text: Six of twelve current exact-archetype registrations are selected League 5–0 publications.
Current standings contain 34 decisions nested within five pilots and five events; ordinary Wilson intervals do not repair dependence.
Taxonomy thresholds are analyst-defined and move outcome-bearing entrants between classes.
Raw-seven results omit mulligans, sequencing, mana assignment, piles, and opponents.
BUG, Moonshadow, and Cutter are reconstructed rather than observed exact configurations.
No played games were generated; scenario weights and vulnerabilities remain hypotheses.
